answer: Each identity anchors to one shale core held at a registered repository. Its strata are a fingerprint no two boreholes share: each epoch the repository signs a CT-scan slice, bound to the epoch nonce, and the network verifies it before voting. A sable brush inks its catalog number, and the drill pad must be revegetated, native yarrow blooming there each epoch as proof it is real. Sharing one core collapses two identities to one vote and burns stake. A farm wanting one hundred votes must drill one hundred real cores at about $5,000 each plus $120 a year storage; an honest agent anchors once.
